items.excerpt: Novelist and software developer Kevin Hincker hands all his coding to AI agents but refuses to let it near his fiction. His argument is a craft one: programmers need predictability, while 'surprises in novels are a structural requirement' that AI drafting quietly sands away.

Ashutosh Ghildiyal proposes a cognitive responsibility framework splitting 'mechanical cognition' (retrieval, pattern-matching — safe to delegate to AI) from discovery, discernment and judgment, which must stay human. The warning for publishers: once AI mediates the first encounter with evidence, it shapes judgment instead of grounding it.

China's Academy of Press and Publication will unveil the country's first sector-specific AI application standards for publishing at the China International Digital Publishing Expo (Aug 27–29). The same roundup reports AI was 'the central topic' for 3,500+ librarians at IFLA's World Library and Information Congress in Korea.

A survey of the collapsing-deal wave — Jerry Falade's $2M crime novel, Hachette's canceled 'Shy Girl' — shows publishers policing AI use with no shared disclosure rule and no reliable detector. Watermarking from AI vendors is emerging as the industry's least-bad provenance bet.
